description: Just a person who wants to build something fun
summary:
Lunar Navigator is an interactive mission planning platform that simplifies lunar exploration. Currently, evaluating Moon landing sites requires manually cross-referencing complex elevation maps with dense astronomical data.

To solve this, we developed a 3D lunar globe with a built-in AI assistant that translates this heavy data into clear, side-by-side visual comparisons. Instead of wrestling with spreadsheets, mission teams can rapidly test multiple scenarios, simulate rover paths, and quickly find backup options if launch dates shift.

This tool is vital for upcoming missions to the lunar South Pole, where the Sun hovers just 1.5 degrees above the horizon. In this extreme environment, a single crater shadow can freeze a lander or cut off communications with Earth. If plans change, Lunar Navigator instantly recalculates sunlight windows and radio signals across dozens of landing sites.

By turning weeks of manual calculations into instant visual insights, Lunar Navigator helps planners, scientists, and engineers safely and confidently map out humanity’s return to the Moon.
details:
Project Description & Mechanics

  • Unified Simulation Platform: Combines 3D lunar mapping with real-time solar system tracking to evaluate safe landing zones and surface operations.
  • Shadow & Line-of-Sight Mapping: Instantly checks Sun and Earth positions against local crater topography to flag dangerous shadows or communication blackouts.
  • Real-Time Time Scrubber: A smooth, lag-free timeline controller that lets users scrub through a full lunar month, watching shadows, temperatures, and Earth visibility shift dynamically.
  • Comparative Analysis Deck: Allows users to view multiple candidate landing sites side-by-side, comparing terrain slopes, solar energy availability, and radio link strength.
  • Deep-Dive Telemetry Inspector: Features cross-section views of craters to identify safe, flat landing shelves and check precise radio signal margins.
  • Dynamic Mission Modeling: Simulates battery life, power drain, and rover driving speeds based on the selected mission profile (e.g., crewed, rover, static lander) and local terrain.
  • Integrated AI Assistant: Features "Dr. Raj, Ph.D Astrophysicists " an AI advisor powered by live map telemetry to help planners identify hazards and answer operational queries on the fly.

Key Benefits

  • Consolidated Workflow: Replaces the need to jump between separate NASA databases and complex math scripts by computing everything instantly in one dashboard.
  • Instant Adaptability: Allows planners to simply slide the timeline to a new date to see the immediate impact on sunlight and communications if a launch gets delayed.
  • Offline Reliability: Runs core physics directly on the user's device, ensuring the timeline and site analysis function smoothly even if the internet connection drops.
  • Broad Accessibility: Uses an intuitive, color-coded interface for students and educators while maintaining the strict decimal-precision physics required by actual aerospace engineers.

Intended Impact

  • Mission Safety: Protects multi-million-dollar equipment and astronauts at the treacherous lunar South Pole by clearly visualizing when life-threatening shadows will occur.
  • Accelerated Planning: Helps science teams rapidly balance their desire to explore difficult, icy terrain with the engineering need for safe, flat, well-lit landing spots.
  • Educational Outreach: Democratizes space exploration by giving students and enthusiasts access to the same data and planning challenges faced by NASA professionals.

Tools & Technologies

  • Frontend: JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, paired with Three.js for an interactive 3D Moon globe using high-resolution surface textures.
  • Backend: Python using the FastAPI framework to manage data requests and routing.
  • AI Integration: Google Gemini API customized to interpret live aerospace telemetry.
  • Authentic Data Sources: Powered by real NASA datasets, including LROC imagery, LOLA elevation models, Diviner temperature data, and JPL Horizons planetary tracking.

Creative Innovations

  • Visualized Geometry: Transforms complex 3D math into simple, 2D "skyline" graphs where users can literally watch the Sun and Earth dip behind local crater peaks.
  • Immersive Interface: Designed to mimic a real mission control console, featuring target crosshairs, live readouts, and clear safety warnings.
  • On-the-Fly Synthesis: Allows users to click anywhere on the 3D globe—not just pre-selected sites—to instantly generate local terrain, temperature, and sunlight data for that exact spot.
  • Dual-Persona AI: The AI dynamically switches tones, acting as a strict, data-driven Flight Director for engineers or a friendly Planetary Scientist for educational use.

Design Considerations

  • Harsh Environmental Factors: Accounted for the Moon's natural wobble (libration), freezing crater temperatures, and far-side communication blackouts requiring relay satellites.
  • Hardware Limitations: Programmed with strict landing gear tilt constraints, flagging slopes as safe, risky, or hazardous based on real spacecraft engineering limits.
  • System Reliability: Built with a decoupled software architecture where the globe, timeline, and data cards communicate seamlessly without slowing down the application, backed by rigorous automated math testing.
